audit_notes: Parameter check: lamella h for a 25 mm plate at 2 m/s: Re = 2*0.025/1.6e-5 = 3100, Nu = 0.664 Re^0.5 Pr^(1/3) = 33, h = 33*0.026/0.025 = 34 W/m2K per side; 30 W/m2K is fair (lower in calm afternoons, ~15). Shading fraction 0.85 on a west wall requires lamella spacing/depth tuned for low afternoon sun; plausible for vertical fins or dense lamellae. The air behind the screen is sheltered: h at the wall drops to ~12 W/m2K (the formulator's change); this is included and slightly raises the wall temperature for a given absorbed flux. The shaded wall loses most of its sky view, so its net longwave loss drops (modelled with (1-shading_fraction)). Dimensionless: lamella Reynolds number 3100 (laminar), Nusselt 33, Biot of envelope 0.044. Simulation coefficient: lamella excess temperature alpha_l*I*sf/(2*h_l) = 0.3*300*0.85/60 = 1.3 K. Model: steady 1D conduction, analytical. Baseline: exposed wall with aged cool paint (h_o 20 W/m2K, no shading). Expected gain ~16%. Mechanical: screen must be designed for wind loads (~1 kPa) and fixings for 20 years; standard for brise-soleil. Audit passed.
